tasks.short: Develop content ideas that fit audience needs and marketing priorities.

steps.what: Review audience results and recurring questions in the {BI}.
Read campaign briefs, previous content and source material in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved campaign brief, audience signals and selected archive documents.
loop.output: Opportunity notes with source references and missing information.
loop.check: Verify document permissions and source references; editor checks interpretation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per pack; unreadable or unsupported material returns to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant audience problems and previous coverage are expressed in free text.

steps.what: Write possible angles and audience benefits in an idea shortlist.

loop.input: Reviewed opportunity notes, campaign constraints and source pack.
loop.output: Up to six proposed angles with audience benefit, evidence and open questions.
loop.check: Check required fields and source references; editor judges originality and audience relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; weak ideas are discarded or developed manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules can format ideas but cannot produce useful alternative angles from varied material.

steps.what: Discuss promising angles and source availability with the marketing team.
Select an angle and record its content brief in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure the {BI} to collect audience signals and use a bounded reading loop over authorised material in the {DOCS}. A second bounded loop drafts an idea shortlist; the editor discusses the angles and approves a content brief in the {PROJECT}. Templates carry the selected angle, evidence and open questions into the writer's assignment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audience evidence was scattered, and idea quality depended on editorial judgement. Templates helped with structure but did little to interpret varied source material.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting handles structured signals. Bounded reading and drafting can prepare alternatives, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting exports and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Original angles, weak audience evidence and access to credible sources still require editorial work. Fluent drafts can hide unsupported assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a compelling audience problem and rejecting familiar ideas that add little.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of a content angle addressing an unanswered audience question

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time assembling evidence and drafting initial options, and more time testing angles with colleagues. Formal commissioning rights stay unchanged unless the marketing manager delegates them.

reach.task: Translate recurring audience questions into research hypotheses.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, question coding and how to distinguish a signal from a vocal minority.

evidence.claim: Bounded drafting can improve some professional writing tasks; the trial does not establish content-idea quality.
Archive question answering and simpler wording are being tested in editorial settings.
Audience judgement and selection remain substantial parts of marketing ideation.

assumptions: The editor works on company publications and campaign content rather than an independent newsroom.
The supplied near-total automation prior is too optimistic: discussion, originality and selection remain human.
Audience reporting exists, and approved source packs can be exported.
Build ranges cover a small reusable workflow, not a new reporting platform.
GDPR applies to audience data; marketing work does not receive a general journalistic exemption.
unknowns: Available audience datasets and their permitted uses.
Archive access, source rights and retention requirements.
Who can commission content and approve campaign priorities.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Does the shortlist improve audience relevance when editors assess suggestions without knowing their origin?
Which recurring audience questions lack suitable existing content?
How often do proposed angles contain unsupported assumptions?
new_work: Review source references and discard weak suggested angles.
Maintain approved source collections and brief templates.
Check access controls and repair failed data imports.
Compare selected ideas with subsequent audience results.

tasks.short: Allocate print space among text, photographs and illustrations.

steps.what: Read page limits, print specifications and layout rules in the {DOCS}.
Rank approved copy and artwork by significance and reader needs.
Measure text fit and artwork dimensions in {OTHER} layout software.
Arrange text and images into a layout proof using {OTHER} layout software.
Review the layout proof for emphasis, readability and image treatment.
Apply corrections in {OTHER} layout software and export a revised proof.
Approve the revised layout proof in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Store page constraints and layout rules in the {DOCS}, then use deterministic scripts in {OTHER} layout software to measure fit and populate approved templates. The desktop publisher adjusts composition, and the editor reviews emphasis and readability before approving the exact proof in the {PROJECT}. No model loop is needed for the initial scope.
tasks.previous_blocker: Template automation existed, but constraints, copy and artwork were inconsistent. Bespoke layout scripts and file exchanges required specialist effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing layout engines can measure rendered text and populate templates. AI-assisted coding makes the import, fit checks and correction controls cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Visual balance, meaningful crops and unusual compositions need skilled judgement. Reliable automation depends on layout scripting access and stable fonts.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing what deserves prominence and judging the reader's visual path.

ambition.what: Readers needing a large-print edition of the company publication

tasks.altitude: The editor and desktop publisher spend less time measuring and rebuilding routine layouts. Existing layout approval rights remain; a large-print pilot requires a separate scope and budget decision.

reach.task: Design reusable publication grids and accessible large-print variants.
reach.learn: Typographic hierarchy, image cropping, contrast and print accessibility.

evidence.claim: Layout engines support deterministic text fitting, template population and technical checks.
Editorial significance and visual composition still require human judgement.

assumptions: Print allocation is relevant to a company magazine, brochure or report; many marketing editors do it only periodically.
A desktop publisher implements layouts while the editor controls editorial emphasis.
Templates and stable fonts cover a useful share of pages.
The model-needed prior is reduced because rendering and fit calculations are deterministic.
Build ranges cover one publication format; the large-print pilot is additional work.
unknowns: Scripting and export capabilities of the existing {OTHER} layout software.
Font licences, artwork permissions and supported print formats.
Number of exceptional page designs and late copy changes.
Demand and budget for a large-print edition.
research_questions: Which recurring page types can be populated without weakening visual quality?
How closely do automated fit reports match final printed output?
Which reader needs justify a separate large-print format?
new_work: Maintain templates, font settings and fit rules.
Inspect overflow, poor crops and unusual compositions.
Recheck rendering after layout software or font changes.
Develop and validate accessibility rules for any new edition.

tasks.short: Agree story placement and emphasis with management and editorial colleagues.

steps.what: Review developing stories, deadlines and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Prepare placement options and unresolved questions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Current content briefs, agenda, campaign brief and space constraints.
loop.output: Briefing with placement options, conflicts and questions linked to source material.
loop.check: Validate dates and capacity deterministically; editor checks framing and omitted concerns.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; ambiguous priorities are left as questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Story emphasis and conflicting priorities are described in free text.

steps.what: Discuss placement, emphasis and sensitive issues with management and editorial colleagues.
Agree placement and emphasis, resolving competing priorities.
Record the editorial decision and assignments in the {PROJECT}.
Send agreed assignments and changes through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} to assemble an agenda and capture approved decisions through a structured form. A bounded loop prepares a source-linked briefing in the {DOCS}; people discuss the options and the marketing manager approves placement and emphasis. That approval updates the editorial plan and triggers internal notices through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The conversation depended on context and trust, while preparation and follow-up were fragmented. Treating the meeting as one indivisible task concealed the simpler administrative steps.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, dashboards and notifications can handle the structured work. A bounded drafting loop can prepare free-text material without taking decision authority.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive company news and disagreements over emphasis require discussion. Decisions made outside the structured form still need someone to enter them.
tasks.human_edge: Surfacing disagreement, reading organisational context and negotiating a defensible editorial choice.

ambition.what: A midweek placement review for developing company news

tasks.altitude: The editor arrives with clearer options and spends less time circulating decisions. Management keeps its approval rights; the editor gains preparation capacity, with no automatic change in formal authority.

reach.task: Assess timing and emphasis for sensitive company announcements.
reach.learn: Stakeholder mapping, announcement dependencies and reputational trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Structured agendas, decision forms and internal notifications can use existing workflow configuration.
Professional writing research supports assistance with briefing preparation, not replacement of editorial negotiation.

assumptions: Developing news means company announcements and publication stories in this marketing setting.
The marketing manager resolves competing priorities; the editor prepares and records the decision.
No meeting recording or individual productivity scoring is needed.
The human-task prior remains appropriate for discussion and decisions, while preparation and follow-up can change.
GDPR applies; consultation and employee participation requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Actual placement approval rights and escalation paths.
Whether sensitive briefs may enter an approved model environment.
How often decisions happen outside scheduled discussions.
National rules and existing employee agreements affecting the implementation.
research_questions: Which briefing fields most often prevent repeated discussion?
Does an additional short review improve placement decisions enough to justify meeting time?
Can structured decision entry replace minutes for this workflow?
new_work: Review briefing framing and missing concerns.
Enter decisions and exceptions in the structured form.
Maintain approval routes and notification recipients.
Remove superseded or sensitive briefing material according to retention rules.

tasks.short: Coordinate publication production against deadlines, quality requirements and budgets.

steps.what: Set production milestones, owners and dependencies in the {PROJECT}.
Reconcile supplier quotes and expected costs against the budget in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Request artwork, layout and printing progress through the {EMAIL}.
Check artwork and typeset files using preflight in {OTHER} layout software.
Resolve deadline, quality and cost exceptions with contributors and suppliers.
Review the final proof, costs and resolved exceptions in the {DOCS}.
Authorise release and submit the print order through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Record print confirmation and archive released files in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} for milestone templates, contributor status updates and exception alerts, and reconcile structured quotes with commitments from the {ERP} on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Preflight in {OTHER} layout software and versioned files in the {DOCS} assemble a release pack for editorial review. A deterministic connection submits the print order through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} only after approval of the exact files, quantity and price; confirmation feeds the publication record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress lived in mail threads, costs in separate records and production files in changing folders. External printing interfaces and inconsistent identifiers made reliable handoffs expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Milestone workflows and preflight checks already exist. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of matching records and building a narrow order connection, where supported access is available.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier delays, late artwork and quality disputes still require negotiation. Portal access and reliable quote matching can dominate implementation effort.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating a workable recovery plan and deciding whether the final publication is ready to release.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly deadline-risk decisions for active publications

tasks.altitude: The editor spends less time chasing updates and copying figures, and more time resolving threatened deadlines. Existing release and spending limits remain; approval above those limits follows the company's current route.

reach.task: Compare publication timing and production costs with campaign priorities.
reach.learn: Campaign dependencies, supplier lead times and budget trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Milestone tracking, reminders, preflight and archiving primarily need configuration and deterministic integration.
Supplier negotiation and final release judgement remain human responsibilities.

assumptions: The editor coordinates a recurring printed marketing publication rather than operating printing equipment.
A {SPREADSHEET} commonly joins quotes and commitments even when the {ERP} holds financial records.
Contributors maintain structured status fields; this work is included in new_work.
Supplier quotes use structured fields or are entered into a form; free-text extraction is outside the initial scope.
The editor can authorise orders within an existing spending limit.
The {PARTNER_PORTAL} provides supported integration access; otherwise submission stays manual.
GDPR applies, and any consultation concerning employee monitoring follows national rules.
unknowns: Supplier integration access and permitted order submission methods.
Current spending limits, procurement approvals and signatories.
Reliability of supplier identifiers and committed-cost exports.
Whether preflight profiles match each printer's specifications.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Which status fields predict deadline problems early enough to act?
Can print orders be submitted safely with duplicate prevention and receipt verification?
Which technical faults are caught by current preflight profiles?
Does structured status entry reduce total coordination effort across all contributors?
new_work: Contributors update milestone status and flag blocked work.
Review unmatched quotes, cost discrepancies and preflight exceptions.
Maintain supplier mappings, schedules and approval limits.
Verify failed submissions before retrying to prevent duplicate print orders.
Reapprove any changed release files, quantity or price.
Maintain access permissions, logs and archive retention.

role.altitude: The editor's week shifts toward audience choices, editorial discussion, visual judgement and production exceptions. Preparation and administration shrink; formal commissioning, spending and publication rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Market research analysts: turn audience questions into testable content opportunities.
Graphic designers: develop reusable publication grids and accessible formats.
Public relations managers: assess timing and emphasis for sensitive announcements.
Advertising and promotions managers: connect production risks with campaign priorities.
skills_to_grow: Audience evidence assessment and experiment design.
Source verification and review of model drafts.
Print accessibility, layout constraints and preflight interpretation.
Supplier lead-time analysis and cost reconciliation.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an audience-led publication service that combines a weekly unanswered-question review, timely company-news placement and an accessible print edition pilot. Use reusable templates, export adapters and bounded drafting loops; validate demand and quality before expanding the service.
